title: First-year electronics degree — representative circuit/device/digital strand

handoff.scope: Inventory and generation/extraction requirements only. No symbol geometry, device models, footprints or application subfolder feature is implemented.
handoff.folder_semantics: folder is a proposed slash-separated logical path, not a claim of support in the current TinyCAD library browser.
handoff.source_document_base: All source_document paths are relative to the repository root, including in standalone library files.
handoff.identity: id is stable within a library; extraction may deduplicate by canonical_symbol_id, but each library is complete and permits independent duplicate assets.
handoff.pin_contract: Logical terminal numbers and signal names are not physical package pinouts. Resolve real package pins from an authoritative device reference before generating package-specific symbols.
handoff.conventions: Prefer IEC/UK teaching symbols. Power pins and polarity should remain explicit. Built-in instruments, probes, independent waveform sources and voltage-controlled sources are excluded from symbol generation. Use existing_tools configuration with the native tool defaults.
handoff.existing_tools: existing_tools and existing_tool_ids refer to supplied non-library tools, not generation requirements. Never recreate these as library symbols.
handoff.inventory_not_bom: One record per reusable symbol type, not per component instance. A bridge can be assembled from repeated diode/resistor symbols. Different resistance/capacitance values are properties, not separate symbols.
handoff.model_warning: Every record is marked not ready to simulate from this manifest. A successful extraction of artwork does not establish a valid model, mapping or instrument implementation.
handoff.optionality: experiment_symbol_ids are a coverage set of proposed implementations and comparisons, not a minimal mandatory BOM; common support symbols and explicitly optional additions are separately identified.

experiments.title: Nodal and mesh analysis
experiments.catalogue_description: Solve the same network by two analytical methods and compare each node/current with the numerical solution. Use signed reference arrows.

experiments.title: Source superposition
experiments.catalogue_description: Run separate single-source conditions and the full circuit. Compare voltages/currents, and explain why powers cannot simply be superposed.

experiments.title: Thevenin/Norton models
experiments.catalogue_description: Derive a port equivalent and compare original/equivalent circuits across a load sweep. Record port definitions and reference direction.

experiments.title: Sources, loads and power
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary a finite load against explicit source resistance. Compare delivered power and internal dissipation without assuming that maximum power means maximum efficiency.

experiments.title: Meter loading and generator impedance
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare theoretical unloaded values with the actual virtual instruments attached. Include function-generator output resistance and meter burden/input resistance.

experiments.title: RC/RL complete step response
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare initial condition, forced response and final state. Choose capture duration and step from the fastest/slowest relevant time constants.

experiments.title: Impedance and phase
experiments.catalogue_description: Sweep frequency and calculate complex impedance from voltage/current results. Compare magnitude and phase with the analytical prediction.

experiments.title: Resonant network
experiments.catalogue_description: Use a declared RLC topology and vary damping. Compare frequency response with its transient ringing and measure the relevant bandwidth.

experiments.title: Passive filters
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare low/high-pass response using AC analysis, then apply pulses in transient analysis. Explain the effect of loading on the nominal cutoff.

experiments.title: Energy storage and loss
experiments.catalogue_description: Integrate current or component power over a stated interval. Check the energy balance for a capacitor or inductor network against analytical calculations.

experiments.title: Diode characteristic and operating point
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare a chosen SPICE diode with an ideal/piecewise analytical approximation. Examine where the approximation produces an unacceptable error.

experiments.title: Rectification and smoothing
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare half/full-wave circuits and load-dependent ripple with a low-voltage sine source. Include real diode models and use transient analysis.

experiments.title: Transistor bias and load line
experiments.catalogue_description: Predict DC operating point, run the model and repeat for component tolerances. Export device readings for a load-line comparison.

experiments.title: BJT amplifier gain and resistance
experiments.catalogue_description: Measure small-signal gain and infer input/output resistance using controlled source/load changes. Compare with a small-signal equivalent.

experiments.title: FET characteristics and switching
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare selected gate/drain conditions with a device model. Investigate gate-drive and load effects rather than assuming every FET is an ideal switch.

experiments.title: Op-amp feedback stages
experiments.catalogue_description: Compare inverting and non-inverting gain, input loading and output range. Distinguish an ideal analytical block from a model with rails and frequency limits.

experiments.title: Active filter
experiments.catalogue_description: Measure a prepared op-amp filter's gain/phase and pulse response. Compare component changes with the predicted poles/cutoff using an appropriate amplifier model.

experiments.title: Logic functions and minimisation
experiments.catalogue_description: Test a truth table against two alternative gate implementations. Do the Boolean/Karnaugh-map reasoning separately and compare all input combinations.

experiments.title: Multiplexer, decoder and encoder
experiments.catalogue_description: Use compatible component models or a gate-level circuit. Capture outputs while enumerating data/select inputs.

experiments.title: Latch versus edge-triggered flip-flop
experiments.catalogue_description: Apply a defined clock/data sequence and compare stored state. State timing assumptions; ideal models do not establish real setup/hold limits.

experiments.title: Counter and shift register
experiments.catalogue_description: Verify reset and output sequences and compare synchronous/asynchronous operation where delay models permit.

experiments.title: Logic-family loading and propagation
experiments.catalogue_description: Vary capacitance/fan-out within a valid device model. Measure edge and propagation timing. A zero-delay Boolean model is insufficient.

experiments.title: Adder and overflow indication
experiments.catalogue_description: Implement a small gate-level arithmetic example and enumerate operand combinations. Explain signed/unsigned interpretation outside the circuit.

experiments.title: State-machine I/O plan
experiments.catalogue_description: Draw the input/output, clock/reset and state-register interfaces for a small controller. A separate HDL tool is needed to implement, synthesise and verify SystemVerilog.

experiments.title: FPGA/microcontroller interface schematic
experiments.catalogue_description: Record supplies, connectors, pull resistors and external driver stages. TinyCAD does not program an FPGA, execute firmware or replace the course's digital development environment.

experiments.title: Integrated design/test exercise
experiments.catalogue_description: Combine a defined input, conditioner and output stage. Save analytical targets, model identities, captures, loading assumptions and a plan for bench comparison. The project brief is our proposal, not an institution-prescribed assignment.
